sections.filled: Santa Fe sits at about 2,128 m above sea level, in a basin that runs from about 1,436 m to 3,936 m. It lies in the Colorado Plateau shrublands ecoregion. Its basin also takes in parts of the Colorado Rockies forests and Arizona Mountains forests ecoregions.

sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 14,659 km², rainfall averages about 360 mm a year, moderately seasonal, with August the wettest month. Temperatures there average 10.2 °C, from -0.7 °C in January to 21.6 °C in July. Its aridity index of 0.30 falls in the UNEP semi-arid class. Compared with the seven basins around it, its basin receives more precipitation than four, is warmer than four and is more humid than five.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.filled: Across the basin, the land is sloping on average (a mean slope of 9.5%), with topsoil that averages 50% sand, 34% silt and 16% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly unconsolidated sediments. Karst outcrop covers up to about 18% of the basin.

sections.filled: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Santa Fe itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 14,659 km² that contains it, from global datasets.
